issues: What does the common law duty of procedural fairness require of a federal decision-maker cancelling a licence
Whether failure to provide notice of the allegations and an opportunity to respond breaches the duty of fairness
Whether failure to give reasons for cancelling a licence breaches the duty of fairness
What factors determine the content of the duty of fairness owed in a given administrative context (Baker factors)
What remedy is available on judicial review where a decision was made in breach of procedural fairness
Whether the enabling statute or regulations impose specific procedural requirements for licence cancellation
key_facts: A federal decision-maker cancelled the client's licence
The client was not given an opportunity to respond to the allegations against him before cancellation
No reasons were given for the decision
causes_of_action: Application for judicial review on grounds of breach of procedural fairness (denial of right to be heard and failure to give reasons)
candidate_statutes: Statutory Powers Procedure Act (if applicable, though likely not federal)
Enabling federal statute/regulations governing the specific licence (unspecified)

duty to give reasons administrative decision
judicial review remedy breach of fairness
notice and opportunity to respond administrative decision
